events.title: Farming villages along the Nile
events.description: Communities at Merimde and the Fayum grow wheat and barley on land the flood renews each year. Egypt's whole political economy rests on that annual gift.

events.title: Naqada culture emerges
events.description: Upper Egyptian towns develop craft specialisation, long-distance trade and increasingly unequal burials. Wealth is starting to concentrate.

events.title: The first hieroglyphs
events.description: Labels from a tomb at Abydos carry the earliest known Egyptian writing, used first for accounting and ownership rather than literature.

events.title: Upper and Lower Egypt unified
events.description: A ruler recorded as Narmer or Menes joins the two lands. The double crown and the title Lord of the Two Lands outlast every dynasty that follows.

events.title: Memphis founded
events.description: A capital is planted at the junction of valley and delta, where the two halves of the country can be held together and watched.

events.title: The nilometer and the calendar
events.description: Officials record flood heights to forecast the harvest and set taxes. A 365-day solar calendar is in use, the ancestor of our own.

events.title: Djoser's Step Pyramid
events.description: Imhotep stacks six stone mastabas at Saqqara to make the world's first monumental building in cut stone. Architecture becomes a statement of state capacity.

events.title: Sneferu's pyramids at Dahshur
events.description: Three attempts, including one whose angle had to be changed mid-build, work out the engineering. The true pyramid is the result.

events.title: The Great Pyramid at Giza
events.description: Khufu's tomb uses over two million blocks and stays the tallest structure on earth for nearly four thousand years. It is built by paid, fed, organised labour, not slaves.

events.title: The Great Sphinx carved
events.description: A lion with a king's face is cut from the bedrock beside Khafre's causeway. It is later buried to the neck by sand and dug out repeatedly.

events.title: The Pyramid Texts inscribed
events.description: Spells to carry the king through the afterlife are carved inside the pyramid of Unas, the oldest religious writing of any length in the world.

events.title: Provincial governors grow powerful
events.description: Nomarchs build fine tombs in their own districts rather than beside the king. Authority is leaking out of the centre.

events.title: The Old Kingdom collapses
events.description: Low floods, famine and a fragmented court end centralised rule. The First Intermediate Period leaves texts full of disorder and reversal.

events.title: Thebes rises against Herakleopolis
events.description: Two rival dynasties claim Egypt from opposite ends of the valley. The southern house eventually wins.

events.title: Mentuhotep II reunifies Egypt
events.description: The Theban king reunites the country and founds the Middle Kingdom, later remembered as a classical age of language and literature.

events.title: Fortresses in Nubia
events.description: Senusret III garrisons the second cataract with mudbrick fortresses to control gold and trade. Egypt becomes an imperial power southwards.

events.title: The Fayum irrigated
events.description: Canals and a regulated basin turn the Fayum depression into rich farmland. Water management is a royal project, not a local one.

events.title: The Tale of Sinuhe
events.description: A courtier's fictional flight and homecoming becomes the most copied work of Egyptian literature, studied by scribes for a thousand years.

events.title: The Hyksos take the delta
events.description: Rulers of Levantine origin govern Lower Egypt from Avaris, bringing the horse, the chariot and the composite bow.

events.title: Ahmose expels the Hyksos
events.description: The Theban house drives out the delta kings and founds the Eighteenth Dynasty. Egypt now keeps a standing army and campaigns abroad.

events.title: Hatshepsut takes the throne
events.description: Regent for her stepson, she rules as king in her own right for two decades, sends a famous trading expedition to Punt and builds at Deir el-Bahari.

events.title: Thutmose III wins at Megiddo
events.description: A risky march through a narrow pass wins the first battle in history recorded in tactical detail. Seventeen campaigns extend Egypt to the Euphrates.

events.title: Akhenaten's religious revolution
events.description: The king promotes the sun-disc Aten above all gods, closes temples and builds a new capital at Amarna. Art turns strange and intimate.

events.title: Tutankhamun restores the old gods
events.description: A boy king reverses his father's reform and returns the court to Thebes. His obscurity is why his tomb survives largely intact.

events.title: The Battle of Kadesh
events.description: Ramesses II fights the Hittites to a bloody draw and has it carved everywhere as a triumph. State propaganda is already a mature craft.

events.title: The first recorded peace treaty
events.description: Egypt and Hatti sign a treaty of peace and mutual defence, surviving in both Egyptian and Hittite copies. A replica hangs at the United Nations.

events.title: Abu Simbel cut from the cliff
events.description: Four colossal Ramesses figures front a temple aligned so the sun reaches the sanctuary twice a year. It is a border statement aimed at Nubia.

events.title: The first recorded strike
events.description: Tomb workers at Deir el-Medina down tools when their grain rations fail to arrive. The dispute is recorded in detail on ostraca.

events.title: The harem conspiracy against Ramesses III
events.description: Court documents record a plot to kill the king, its trial and its punishments. CT scans of his mummy suggest the assassins succeeded.

events.title: Egypt splits again
events.description: Pharaohs rule from Tanis in the north while the high priests of Amun hold the south. The empire in Asia is gone.

events.title: Libyan dynasties take the throne
events.description: Descendants of settled Libyan soldiers rule Egypt and are absorbed into its culture. Foreign origin becomes normal at the top.

events.title: The Kushite pharaohs
events.description: Kings from Napata in Nubia conquer Egypt and rule as pharaohs, restoring old temples and old styles with the zeal of outsiders.

events.title: The Assyrians sack Memphis
events.description: Esarhaddon's army takes the capital and Ashurbanipal later burns Thebes. Egypt is a battleground between larger powers.

events.title: The Saite revival
events.description: Psamtik I reunites Egypt from Sais using Greek mercenaries and licenses a Greek trading colony at Naucratis. Archaic styles are deliberately revived.

events.title: Necho's canal and the circumnavigation of Africa
events.description: A canal is cut from the Nile towards the Red Sea, and Herodotus reports Phoenician sailors sent by Necho sailing right around Africa.

events.title: Persian conquest
events.description: Cambyses defeats the Egyptians at Pelusium and Egypt becomes a satrapy. It revolts repeatedly over the next two centuries.

events.title: Herodotus visits Egypt
events.description: The Greek historian records what he is told about the pyramids and the priests. He calls the country the gift of the river.

events.title: Independence regained briefly
events.description: Egypt throws off Persian rule for sixty years under native dynasties before being reconquered. It is the last native rule for over two millennia.

events.title: Alexander takes Egypt
events.description: The Macedonian arrives to little resistance, is acclaimed at the oracle of Siwa and orders a new city on the coast.

events.title: Alexandria founded
events.description: Laid out on a grid between sea and lake, it becomes the largest Greek city in the world and the intellectual capital of the Mediterranean.

events.title: Ptolemy I declares himself king
events.description: Alexander's general founds a dynasty that rules for three centuries, speaking Greek and posing as pharaoh in temple reliefs.

events.title: The Library and the Pharos
events.description: A state-funded research institution collects scrolls from everywhere while a lighthouse of enormous height guards the harbour. Both become bywords.

events.title: Eratosthenes measures the earth
events.description: Using shadow angles at Alexandria and Aswan, the librarian calculates the planet's circumference to within a few per cent.

events.title: The Rosetta Stone carved
events.description: A priestly decree is cut in hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek. Two thousand years later it is the key that reopens the language.

events.title: Pompey killed, Caesar arrives
events.description: Egypt is dragged into Rome's civil war. Caesar backs Cleopatra VII against her brother and stays the winter.

events.title: Actium
events.description: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at sea off Greece. The following year both are dead and the dynasty ends.

events.title: Egypt becomes a Roman province
events.description: Ruled as the emperor's personal possession, senators barred from entering without permission. Its grain feeds the city of Rome.

events.title: Christianity reaches Alexandria
events.description: Tradition credits Mark with founding the church there. Egypt becomes one of the most thoroughly Christianised parts of the empire.

events.title: Antony withdraws to the desert
events.description: Egyptian ascetics invent monasticism, first as hermits and then in organised communities under Pachomius. The model spreads across Christendom.

events.title: Pagan temples closed
events.description: Theodosius bans pagan worship; the Serapeum at Alexandria is destroyed. The last hieroglyphic inscription is carved at Philae in 394.

events.title: The Council of Chalcedon splits the church
events.description: Egypt's church rejects the council's formula on Christ's nature and goes its own way as the Coptic Orthodox Church. The rift never closes.

events.title: Persian occupation
events.description: The Sasanians hold Egypt for a decade before Heraclius wins it back. Both empires are exhausted by the effort.

events.title: The Arab conquest
events.description: Amr ibn al-As takes Egypt from a weakened Byzantium and founds a garrison town, Fustat, beside the fortress of Babylon.

events.title: Arabic becomes the language of government
events.description: Administration switches from Greek and Coptic. Conversion is gradual, taxed rather than forced, and takes centuries to reach a majority.

events.title: The Tulunids rule independently
events.description: Ahmad ibn Tulun, sent as governor, stops remitting revenue to Baghdad and builds his own city and mosque. Egypt is a power in its own right again.

events.title: The Fatimids conquer Egypt and found Cairo
events.description: An Ismaili Shia dynasty from the Maghreb takes the country and lays out a royal city, al-Qahira, north of Fustat.

events.title: Al-Azhar founded
events.description: Built as a Fatimid mosque and school, it becomes the most influential centre of Sunni learning after the dynasty falls. It is still operating.

events.title: Al-Hakim destroys the Holy Sepulchre
events.description: The erratic Fatimid caliph's persecution of Christians and Jews is remembered as one provocation among several behind the First Crusade.

events.title: Saladin ends the Fatimid caliphate
events.description: A Kurdish general sent from Damascus takes power, restores Sunni observance and founds the Ayyubid dynasty. Cairo is walled and the Citadel begun.

events.title: Jerusalem retaken at Hattin
events.description: Saladin destroys the crusader army and takes Jerusalem, ruling Egypt and Syria as one state. Egypt funds the campaign.

events.title: The Mamluks seize power
events.description: Slave soldiers defeat the Seventh Crusade at Mansoura, capture the French king and then overthrow their own masters. A self-replacing military caste rules for centuries.

events.title: The Mongols stopped at Ain Jalut
events.description: A Mamluk army halts the Mongol advance in Galilee, the first serious check they suffer. Cairo becomes the centre of the Islamic world by default.

events.title: The Black Death
events.description: Plague kills perhaps a third of the population and returns repeatedly. Villages are abandoned and the irrigation system decays with them.

events.title: The Circassian Mamluks
events.description: A new faction takes over the sultanate and rules until the Ottoman conquest, presiding over a long fiscal decline.

events.title: The sea route to India opens
events.description: Portuguese ships round Africa and bypass Egypt's spice monopoly. The transit revenue that funded the state drains away.

events.title: The Ottoman conquest
events.description: Selim I defeats the Mamluks outside Cairo and hangs the last sultan. Egypt becomes a province governed from Istanbul.

events.title: The Mamluk beys reassert themselves
events.description: The military households the Ottomans defeated re-emerge as the real power, with the governor increasingly a figurehead.

events.title: Ali Bey al-Kabir's near-independence
events.description: A Mamluk bey stops paying tribute, strikes coins in his own name and briefly takes Syria before being betrayed.

events.title: Plague, famine and misrule
events.description: Repeated epidemics and predatory taxation leave the country depopulated and its canals silted. It is a weak state on the eve of an invasion.

events.title: Napoleon invades Egypt
events.description: A French army wins at the Pyramids and occupies Cairo, bringing with it a hundred and sixty scholars to survey the country.

events.title: Nelson destroys the French fleet
events.description: The Battle of the Nile at Aboukir strands Napoleon's army in Egypt and hands Britain control of the eastern Mediterranean.

events.title: The Rosetta Stone found
events.description: French soldiers repairing a fort uncover the trilingual slab. Ceded to Britain in 1801, it lets Champollion crack hieroglyphs in 1822.

events.title: Muhammad Ali takes power
events.description: An Albanian officer manoeuvres himself into the governorship with popular backing and founds a dynasty that lasts until 1952.

events.title: The massacre of the Mamluks
events.description: Muhammad Ali invites the beys to a banquet at the Citadel and has them shot in the passageway out. The old order ends in an afternoon.

events.title: Long-staple cotton introduced
events.description: A new crop transforms the economy into an export monoculture tied to Lancashire's mills, and ties Egypt's fortunes to a single price.

events.title: Egyptian armies invade Syria
events.description: Ibrahim Pasha beats the Ottomans repeatedly and threatens Istanbul. The European powers intervene to force a withdrawal.

events.title: The first railway in Africa
events.description: A line from Alexandria towards Cairo is built by British engineers, part of a wave of infrastructure funded by borrowing.

events.title: The Suez Canal opens
events.description: Ten years of forced and then paid labour join the Mediterranean to the Red Sea. Egypt gains a strategic asset and a ruinous debt.

events.title: Britain buys the canal shares
events.description: Bankrupt, Ismail sells Egypt's stake to the British government. Foreign controllers are installed over the country's finances.

events.title: Ismail deposed
events.description: The powers have the sultan remove the khedive over his debts. Humiliation at foreign hands feeds a nationalist movement in the army.

events.title: The Urabi revolt
events.description: Colonel Ahmed Urabi leads officers demanding Egypt for the Egyptians and forces a constitutional cabinet.

events.title: British invasion at Tel el-Kebir
events.description: After bombarding Alexandria, British forces crush Urabi's army in a dawn attack. The occupation is announced as temporary and lasts seventy years.

events.title: Cromer's veiled protectorate
events.description: Egypt keeps its khedive, its ministers and its flag while a British consul-general decides policy. The fiction suits everyone but the Egyptians.

events.title: Reconquest of Sudan
events.description: Kitchener's Anglo-Egyptian army destroys the Mahdist state at Omdurman. Sudan is governed jointly, in practice by Britain.

events.title: The first Aswan Dam
events.description: A masonry dam begins the engineering of the flood that had shaped Egyptian life for five thousand years.

events.title: The Denshawai incident
events.description: Villagers are flogged and hanged after a quarrel with British officers shooting pigeons. The brutality galvanises nationalist opinion.

events.title: Egypt declared a protectorate
events.description: With the Ottomans at war with Britain, the legal fiction is dropped. Martial law and wartime requisitioning follow.

events.title: The 1919 Revolution
events.description: The exile of Saad Zaghlul sets off nationwide strikes and demonstrations joined by women, students, peasants and Copts alike.

events.title: Nominal independence
events.description: Britain unilaterally ends the protectorate while reserving defence, the canal, Sudan and the protection of foreigners. Egypt gets a king and a constitution.

events.title: Tutankhamun's tomb opened
events.description: Howard Carter finds the burial nearly intact. The discovery makes Egyptology global news and sharpens Egyptian arguments about who owns the past.

events.title: The Muslim Brotherhood founded
events.description: Hassan al-Banna starts a movement in Ismailia combining piety, welfare and politics. It becomes the template for Islamist organisation everywhere.

events.title: The Anglo-Egyptian Treaty
events.description: British troops are confined to the canal zone. Egypt joins the League of Nations while the underlying dependence persists.

events.title: El Alamein
events.description: Rommel's advance is halted and then broken in the western desert. The battles are fought on Egyptian soil with little Egyptian say.

events.title: Defeat in Palestine
events.description: The war against the new state of Israel goes badly and the army blames the politicians for corrupt supply contracts. Officers begin conspiring.

events.title: Cairo burns
events.description: Rioters torch hundreds of foreign-owned businesses after British troops kill Egyptian police at Ismailia. The monarchy has lost control.

events.title: The Free Officers coup
events.description: A bloodless army takeover sends King Farouk into exile on his yacht. The monarchy is abolished the following year.

events.title: Nasser takes control
events.description: Nasser sidelines Naguib, bans the Brotherhood after an assassination attempt and negotiates British withdrawal from the canal zone.

events.title: The Suez Crisis
events.description: Nasser nationalises the canal; Britain, France and Israel invade and are forced out by American and Soviet pressure. He emerges the hero of Arab nationalism.

events.title: The United Arab Republic
events.description: Egypt and Syria merge into one state. It lasts three years and is undone by Egyptian domination of the arrangement.

events.title: Sweeping nationalisations
events.description: Banks, insurers and large industry are taken into state hands and land holdings capped. The public sector becomes the employer of first resort.

events.title: The Six-Day War
events.description: Israel destroys the air force on the ground and takes Sinai. The defeat shatters Nasserism and closes the canal for eight years.

events.title: The High Dam completed
events.description: Aswan ends the annual flood, generates power and creates Lake Nasser, drowning Nubian villages and holding back the silt that fertilised the valley.

events.title: The October War
events.description: Egyptian forces storm the Bar Lev Line across the canal. The war ends in a difficult military position but a restored bargaining hand.

events.title: Infitah: the economy opened
events.description: Sadat reverses course towards private and foreign investment. Growth returns along with inequality and a new business elite.

events.title: The bread riots
events.description: Cutting subsidies under IMF advice brings hundreds of thousands onto the streets. The cuts are reversed and no government forgets the lesson.

events.title: Peace with Israel
events.description: The Camp David treaty returns Sinai and makes Egypt the first Arab state to recognise Israel. It is expelled from the Arab League for a decade.

events.title: Sadat assassinated
events.description: Islamist soldiers shoot the president at a military parade. Hosni Mubarak succeeds him and declares an emergency law that lasts thirty years.

events.title: The Luxor massacre
events.description: Militants kill sixty-two people, most of them tourists, at Hatshepsut's temple. Tourism collapses and the insurgency loses public sympathy.

events.title: The revolution and Tahrir Square
events.description: Eighteen days of mass protest end Mubarak's thirty years in power. The army takes over the transition.

events.title: Morsi elected
events.description: The Brotherhood's candidate wins the first genuinely contested presidential election. His year in office is marked by a constitutional crisis.

events.title: The military removes Morsi
events.description: After huge protests the army deposes the president, and hundreds of his supporters are killed clearing sit-ins in Cairo. Abdel Fattah el-Sisi takes power.

events.title: The canal expanded
events.description: A second channel is dug in a year and financed by domestic bond sales. Traffic and revenue fall short of the projections.

events.title: The pound floated
events.description: The currency loses half its value overnight under an IMF programme. Inflation and austerity follow, and so does a wave of megaprojects.

events.title: The New Administrative Capital opens for business
events.description: Ministries begin moving to a new city built in the desert east of Cairo, funded by heavy borrowing against uncertain demand.

events.title: Red Sea attacks cut canal traffic
events.description: Shipping diverts around Africa to avoid Houthi missiles, cutting Suez revenue by more than half and straining an already fragile budget.
